name: Executive function
summary: Executive function is an umbrella for related higher-level processes used in goal-directed regulation, commonly including working-memory updating, shifting and inhibition; the processes are partly shared and partly separable, and no single test or factor structure captures executive functioning in every person or context.

includes: Multiple related cognitive processes involved in goal-directed regulation.
Measurement models, performance tasks, questionnaires and their limits.
Relationships between laboratory measures, everyday functioning and neurodevelopmental conditions.
excludes: A single unitary mental capacity or a moral judgement about effort or character.
Treating one laboratory task, questionnaire score or factor model as the definition of executive function.
Assuming an executive-function profile uniquely diagnoses ADHD, autism or another condition.
Assuming a laboratory task that resembles daily life has proven real-world predictive validity.

claims.text: Common executive-function constructs such as working-memory updating, shifting and inhibition show both shared variance and separability, but studies do not support one factor structure that fits all ages and samples.

A cognitive task's resemblance to an everyday activity does not by itself show that its score predicts real-world functioning; ecological validity requires direct evidence linking test performance to real-world outcomes.

Executive-function difficulties occur across multiple neurodevelopmental conditions and are heterogeneous within diagnoses, so executive-function measures should not be treated as condition-specific diagnostic signatures.
Performance tests and informant questionnaires can capture different aspects of executive functioning and should not be assumed to be interchangeable measures of one underlying deficit.

sources.citation: Miyake A et al. The unity and diversity of executive functions and their contributions to complex frontal lobe tasks. Cognitive Psychology. 2000;41(1):49-100.
Karr JE et al. The unity and diversity of executive functions: A systematic review and re-analysis of latent variable studies. Psychological Bulletin. 2018;144(11):1147-1185.
Suchy Y et al. Pitfalls in research on ecological validity of novel executive function tests: A systematic review and a call to action. Psychological Assessment. 2024;36(4):243-261.
Sadozai AK et al. Executive function in children with neurodevelopmental conditions: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Nature Human Behaviour. 2024;8(12):2357-2366.
Kofler MJ et al. Executive function deficits in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder. Nature Reviews Psychology. 2024;3(10):701-719.

uncertainties.question: Which factor models are valid across ages, cultures, neurotypes and measurement methods?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: A model can look universal when it partly reflects the tasks and population used to construct it.
what_would_reduce_it: Well-powered preregistered replications, measurement-invariance analyses and broader multimethod samples.

uncertainties.question: How well do specific executive-function measures predict person-defined functioning in real environments?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: A laboratory effect may not identify the barrier a person experiences or which support will help.
what_would_reduce_it: Prospective studies directly linking test scores with real-world outcomes, ecological momentary assessment and participatory definitions of useful function.

uncertainties.question: Which executive-function patterns, if any, meaningfully distinguish neurodevelopmental conditions after co-occurrence and within-diagnosis heterogeneity are handled properly?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: Apparent diagnostic profiles can be artefacts of comparison groups, comorbidity or measurement choices.
what_would_reduce_it: Large transdiagnostic studies with rigorous co-occurrence measurement and out-of-sample diagnostic prediction.

uncertainties.question: What do performance tasks and informant questionnaires each measure, and when do differences between them matter?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: Calling both measures 'executive function' can conceal that they may capture different constructs or contexts.
what_would_reduce_it: Multitrait-multimethod validation linked to independent real-world outcomes across varied populations.

perspectives.summary: Executive functions are correlated but partly separable rather than one indivisible faculty.
Claims that an executive-function test is ecologically valid should be based on demonstrated prediction of real-world functioning, not superficial resemblance to daily tasks.
Executive-function differences are distributed across diagnoses and people, so group averages should not be converted into a person's assumed cognitive profile.

relations.note: Executive-function differences are commonly studied in ADHD but are heterogeneous and not synonymous with ADHD.
Executive-function differences are commonly studied in autism but are heterogeneous and not diagnostic of autism.
Sensory load and environmental conditions can alter the demands under which executive performance is observed; this relation does not assert one causal mechanism.

questions: Which demand is externalised or reduced?
What setup and maintenance burden remains?
Is transfer to everyday outcomes demonstrated?
Are privacy and notification burdens acceptable?
Can instructions, time, sequencing or interruption demands be redesigned?
Does advice distinguish inability, overload, competing demands and motivation?
Is failure blamed on the user?

provenance.method: Candidate-only Batch B re-review of the original five concepts using foundational, systematic-review and transdiagnostic executive-function evidence; not promoted to the authoritative corpus.
